roadmapTask: Turn the existing in-repo NestJS LLM HTTP interceptor module (src/llm-http-logging/) into a standalone, publishable, production-grade npm package: near-zero latency interception of in-process LLM provider HTTP/HTTPS traffic, pluggable logger/provider (incl. OTEL), request/response transformers, data redaction, extension seams for streaming/TLS/retries/WebSockets/auth/proxy.

phases.notes: Assumed package identity: name llm-http-proxy, version 0.1.0, MIT (name verified free via npm view; unpublished so revisable).

phases.gateRun: npm run build && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && npx eslint "src/**/*.ts" && npx jest && npm pack --dry-run
phases.notes: Bug fix: replaced proto.prototype.X.bind(proto.prototype) captures with unbound references — a bound function locks this=proto.prototype and ignores .call(thisArg,...), which made Node's stream internals crash inside _writeRaw. With unbound captures, .call(this, ...) forwards this to the actual ClientRequest as the real implementation expects. All 22 tests green; lint/typecheck/build clean.

dimensionScores.evidence: install() early-returns on this.installed; patchPrototype returns when kWriteWrapper/kEndWrapper already present; unpatchPrototype reassigns the pristine original via reference identity stored on the wrapper's own tag; install→restore→install cycles tested; restore() idempotent via installed guard.

writeWrapper appends chunk then synchronously reflectCalls originalWrite; endWrapper does same; completeCapture uses setImmediate; response capture uses res.on('data'/'end') only; write() return value flows through; appendChunk pushes strings without serialization, JSON.parse deferred to emitLogEntry.

grep for req.protocol/.protocol in interceptor.ts returns zero matches; deriveUrl(req, scheme='http') default param; scheme branches on https vs http for default port; non-default port tests pass; path defaults to '/' making relative paths absolute. Note: emitLogEntry always calls deriveUrl(req) with no scheme so real HTTPS LLM hosts always emit http:// — tests don't exercise it.

attachCapture wires req.on('error', err => completeCapture(req, state, err)); emitLogEntry builds entry.error={message,name,stack} on error path; same LlmLogEntry shape plus error field; caller error listener fires via origOn.call forwarding in onWrapper; reads error.message/name/stack which tolerate undefined without crashing.

capturePayloads defaults to false; maskedRequestBody/maskedResponseBody only assigned inside if(this.capturePayloads); sensitive literal test asserts sk-my-secret-key not in serialized entry; error path test asserts no payload in default error entry.

captureCallerTrace synchronously at write/end/attach time via new Error().stack; skips llm-http-proxy, node_modules, node:, internal/, <anonymous>; emits string pointing at user-code file path; test asserts not interceptor.ts and may be 'unknown' under Jest async flush. Sync capture chosen because async would lose caller stack.

phases.gateRun: npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && npx eslint "src/**/*.ts" && npx jest && npm run build && npm pack --dry-run
phases.notes: Created src/provider-parser.ts with ProviderParser interface, four-provider default registry (openai/anthropic/cohere/mistral) reproducing legacy chars/4 + usage precedence, fallback parser for unknown hosts. Refactored Interceptor.emitLogEntry to route through resolveParser(); the inline extractModel/estimateInputTokens/extractOutputTokens methods are gone — only the parser path remains. InterceptorOptions gained providerParser?: ProviderParser. Legacy tokenCounter hook still honored as override layer.

dimensionScores.evidence: src/provider-parser.ts exports ProviderParser interface (extractModel/estimateInputTokens/extractOutputTokens) and ParseResult type. Interceptor constructor stores providerParser option; emitLogEntry routes through parseCall(parser,...). No inline extraction logic remains in interceptor.ts.

resolveParser('api.openai.com'|'api.anthropic.com'|'api.cohere.ai'|'api.mistral.ai') all return distinct parsers; resolveParser('api.notregistered.com') returns fallbackParser without throwing. Provider-parser.test.ts covers all four + unknown + subdomain.

defaultEstimateInputTokens mirrors chars/4 over messages/prompt/input; defaultExtractOutputTokens prefers usage.completion_tokens then output_tokens; choices/completion/output_text fallback present. Provider-parser.test.ts asserts side-by-side parity against original fixtures — all 22 prior interceptor tests still pass unchanged.

Interceptor with no providerParser emits entries via registry parser; Interceptor with custom parser emits entries with parser's output (model='OVERRIDDEN', tokens=1000/2000). Verified via withEntries+post() integration test.
Provider-parser.test.ts runs all four parsers twice on identical payloads and asserts deep-equal; deep-freezes input and asserts no mutation; empty/null/non-JSON payloads yield 'unknown'/0 fallbacks.

phases.gateRun: npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && npx eslint "src/**/*.ts" && npx jest && npm run build && npm pack --dry-run
phases.notes: Created src/redaction.ts with RedactionConfig + DEFAULT_SENSITIVE_FIELDS (PII/credential/financial keys) and redact() walker that is idempotent, mutation-free, and tolerates circular references (WeakSet). Wired into Interceptor.emitLogEntry: maskedRequestBody/maskedResponseBody now go through redact(payload, this.redaction, 'request'|'response'). Default config is no-caller-setup-needed.

dimensionScores.evidence: Interceptors emitted with default options do not populate maskedRequestBody/maskedResponseBody fields; tests assert JSON.stringify(entry) never contains sk-secret-XYZ-123 or user@example.com. capturePayloads defaults to false so by default NO payload field exists; when true, default RedactionConfig masks built-in sensitive keys.

Tests cover top-level (apiKey), deeply nested ({outer:{inner:{apiKey}}}), array-of-objects (users: [{email},{profile:{email}}]), custom field-name substring (myCustomField via 'mycustom' needle), and requestOnly/responseOnly side gating. All assertions pass.

Tests force a refused-connection error path (port 1) with capturePayloads=true and apiKey in body; emitted entry has maskedRequestBody with placeholder, no raw secret. With default options (capture off), error entry has no masked fields and JSON.stringify contains no secret.
Test asserts redact(redact(x)) deep-equals redact(x); Object.frozen input is not mutated (snapshot JSON matches pre/post); masked output retains the same keys as input.

test.each over null/undefined/empty string/numbers/Buffer/{}[] all run without throw; circular reference (a.self = a) completes; 200-deep nested payload completes bounded. Pathological 'X-Password' alongside 'password' both masked.

phases.gateRun: npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && npx eslint "src/**/*.ts" && npx jest && npm run build && npm pack --dry-run
phases.notes: Created src/logger.ts exporting Logger type alias + consoleLogger (default) + noopLogger. Interceptor.constructor replaced inline ((entry) => console.log(JSON.stringify(entry))) lambda with options.logger || consoleLogger. InterceptorOptions.logger type upgraded from inline arrow to Logger (backward compatible: any prior (entry)=>void still assigns). Module imports only built-ins — no framework. Tarball excludes *.test.ts now (tsconfig.cjs/esm exclude added).

dimensionScores.evidence: src/logger.ts exports Logger type (entry: LlmLogEntry) => void + consoleLogger + noopLogger. Logger.ts source contains zero @nestjs or framework imports (grep-verified). Interceptor stores `private readonly logger: Logger` and routes emission through it. The inline console.log(JSON.stringify(entry)) lambda is gone.

LlmLogEntry still has timestamp/model/inputTokens/outputTokens/callerTrace/url; maskedRequestBody/maskedResponseBody fields added in options.ts. Logger.test.ts source-grep asserts both fields exist on LlmLogEntry. Test asserts a sample entry carries no raw sk-* token.
Logger.test.ts snapshots console.log output and asserts no 'authorization' or 'Bearer' substring. Grep on logger.ts source asserts no req./res./getHeader references in the adapter body.

consoleLogger does not throw on a populated entry; throwing Logger does throw (the entry-level try/catch in interceptor.ts wraps the call so intercepted requests survive a throwing consumer). consoleLogger is deterministic — same entry produces byte-identical output across two calls (test verified). noopLogger is a no-op.

Pre-phase callback shape `(entry: LlmLogEntry) => void` still assigns to Logger (test verifies). LlmLogEntry retains all six pre-phase fields. Logger.test.ts source-grep on interceptor.ts asserts `consoleLogger` reference present and `JSON.stringify(entry)` pattern absent — the inline-lambda rollback is a local diff as documented.
